clue.text: American money tied up in an English abbey

parts.note: a buck is slang for a US dollar
fast means firmly fixed, as a boat made fast

explanation.surface: Dollars are locked away in the coffers of an English monastery.
explanation.walkthrough: Buckfast Abbey is a Benedictine monastery in Devon, known for its tonic wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Buckfast is the name of a working Benedictine monastery in Devon, England.

clue.text: Man on the board calling for a hot drink

explanation.surface: A chess piece or a board member asks for something warming.
explanation.walkthrough: The board is a chessboard; the second sense is an old mulled drink of port, oranges and spices.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop is a chess piece, and also a traditional mulled port punch served warm.

clue.text: Wanted can-opener and created a rumpus to get it

indicators.note: the opener of the word can is its first letter

parts.note: to rave is to rant and make a noisy fuss

explanation.surface: Someone desperate for a tin-opener kicked up a fuss to get one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can-opener' reads as a kitchen tool but gives only the first letter of 'can'.
explanation.definitionFit: To crave something is to long for it, so craved is a synonym of desired.

clue.text: Using softer wood

indicators.note: the letters of softer are put to use in a new order, treated as raw material to rework

explanation.surface: Choosing a less hard timber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Using' is an unusual anagram signal: the letters of SOFTER are employed to build a different word.
explanation.definitionFit: A forest is a large area of trees, a synonym of woodland.

clue.text: An urban area that is part country

parts.note: to sunder is to split or separate, as to part
land is a nation or country

explanation.surface: A town described as belonging partly to the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: Sunderland is a city in north-east England. 'part' looks like a noun but is the verb to separate.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunderland is a city on the River Wear in north-east England, a built-up urban place.

clue.text: Dreads becoming more melancholy

indicators.note: the letters of Dreads become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone who fears things grows gloomier.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadder is the comparative of sad, so it means more gloomy or more unhappy.

clue.text: Really cut a dash when a partner's around

indicators.note: the partner word goes around the scrambled letters

parts.note: an ally is a partner; the 's is 'is'

indicators.note: dash as a verb means to smash, so the letters of cut a are broken and rearranged

explanation.surface: Truly impressing when one's spouse is there to see it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut a dash' looks like the idiom for looking stylish, but 'dash' scrambles the words before it into CTUA, and 'around' wraps the partner word round that.
explanation.definitionFit: Actually and really are synonyms, both meaning in fact or truly.

clue.text: Offering to serve the people

parts.note: to do is to serve or suffice, as in 'that will do'
a nation is a people united by country

explanation.surface: A gift given in order to help the public.
explanation.definitionFit: A donation is a gift, something offered to a cause or charity.

clue.text: Uneasy, having no support

parts.note: a rest is a support, such as an arm rest
-less means without, so no

explanation.surface: Feeling anxious because nothing holds one up.
explanation.walkthrough: Pieces go in answer order: REST then LESS, though the clue gives 'no' first.
explanation.definitionFit: Restless means unable to settle, a synonym for agitated or uneasy.

clue.text: Produce notes about fish fighting

indicators.note: the singing word goes about, that is around, the fish

parts.note: to sing is to produce musical notes
a parr is a young salmon

explanation.surface: Making music around fish that are in combat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Produce' looks like farm goods, but 'Produce notes' is a verb phrase for making music; the parr is a young salmon.
explanation.definitionFit: Sparring is practice boxing, so it means fighting or arguing.

clue.text: Makes little of daring manoeuvres

explanation.surface: Belittles risky acrobatic feats.
explanation.definitionFit: To stunt growth is to keep something small; stunts are also feats of daring.

clue.text: The boss reads love-poetry with some hesitation

parts.note: love is nil in tennis scoring, so the letter O
verse is poetry
er is the sound of someone hesitating

explanation.surface: A manager recites romantic poems, stumbling a little.
explanation.definitionFit: An overseer is a supervisor, someone in charge of workers.

clue.text: Stick by trainee, but colour

parts.note: paste is glue, something that sticks
L is for learner, as on British L-plates for trainee drivers

explanation.surface: A glue stick sits next to an apprentice, yet it is about colour.
explanation.walkthrough: L-plates are the red L signs a learner driver must display in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastel is a soft pale shade, so a kind of colour.

clue.text: He wrote the novel "the cornets"

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of the cornets take a new order

explanation.surface: An author titled a book about brass instruments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book but means new, an anagram signal. G. K. Chesterton wrote the Father Brown stories.
explanation.definitionFit: G. K. Chesterton was an English author, so he is a writer.

clue.text: Everything — everything — included in show arranged for November 1st

parts.note: all means everything

indicators.note: the second all is placed inside the reworked show
the letters of show are arranged into a new order

parts.note: all again means everything

explanation.surface: A show staged for the start of November that includes absolutely everything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' makes HOWS, and 'included in' places the second 'everything' inside it. All Hallows Eve is the night before, Halloween.
explanation.definitionFit: All Hallows, or All Saints' Day, is the Christian feast on the first of November.

clue.text: Youngster holding a certain Greek character to be a awful beast

indicators.note: the youngster word holds the Greek letter inside it

parts.note: a minor is a person under legal age
tau is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A child gripping a Greek figure turns out to be a monster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' suggests a person from a myth, but it is a letter of the alphabet; 'a certain' only dresses the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The Minotaur is the bull-headed monster of Greek myth, a terrible creature.

clue.text: Suffering and in pain

indicators.note: and is placed inside the word for pain

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain
taken as written

explanation.surface: Enduring hardship and hurting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suffering' means tolerating, as in 'can't stand it', not being in pain.
explanation.definitionFit: To stand something is to tolerate it, so standing means enduring or putting up with.

clue.text: In a position to set an example

parts.note: taken as written
a stance is a posture or position

explanation.surface: Being well placed to lead by example.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a case or illustration, so a synonym of example.

clue.text: Camping with the head is mind-bending!

parts.note: someone camping is in a tent
a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness or Sheerness

explanation.surface: Going camping with the boss sounds mind-blowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mind-bending' is read literally: bending the mind to a task, that is concentrating.
explanation.definitionFit: Intentness is fixed concentration, the state of applying one's thoughts hard.

clue.text: Design and erect a new building

indicators.note: a new building of the letters of erect a puts them in another arrangement

explanation.surface: An architect plans and puts up a fresh structure.
explanation.definitionFit: To design something is to devise and make it, a synonym of create.

clue.text: Practise chicanery, from the western point of view

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for west
an angle is a viewpoint or slant

explanation.surface: Cheating, as seen from the perspective of the West.
explanation.definitionFit: To wangle is to obtain something by trickery or manipulation.

clue.text: Regret taking exercise in break

indicators.note: the exercise letters go in the break

parts.note: a rent is a tear or break
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Being sorry for doing a workout during a rest period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' looks like a rest from work but means a tear in cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: To repent is to feel remorse for something done, so it means to regret.

clue.text: Fancy there's some point in talk

indicators.note: the point goes in the talk word

parts.note: to orate is to talk pompously
N, north, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Imagine a speech with a point to it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fancy' looks like the verb to imagine but is the adjective elaborate.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate means elaborately decorated, which is what fancy means as an adjective.

clue.text: Iron reduction

explanation.surface: Pressing clothes cuts things down.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Iron' as de-crease: ironing takes the creases out.
explanation.definitionFit: Ironing takes the creases out of cloth; a decrease is also a drop or lessening.

clue.text: The continental city's name is being changed

indicators.note: the letters of name is are changed into another order

explanation.surface: A European city is getting a new name.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', so the definition reads 'The continental city is'. Amiens is a city in northern France.
explanation.definitionFit: Amiens is a city in northern France, on the European mainland.

clue.text: Restrict the cash in irregular situation

indicators.note: the money letter goes inside the word for odd

parts.note: something in an irregular situation is strange, out of the ordinary
L stands for the pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Limiting spending when circumstances are unusual.
explanation.walkthrough: L goes inside STRANGE before the final E. The pound sign derives from L for libra.
explanation.definitionFit: To strangle something is to choke or suppress it, so to restrict it severely.

clue.text: Far from smartly dressed, and so made fun of

explanation.surface: Someone shabbily turned out and therefore teased.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragged clothes are tattered and scruffy; to rag someone is to tease them.

clue.text: Profits when concern is shown

explanation.surface: Gains appear when people care about something.
explanation.definitionFit: Interest is the return earned on money lent, and also curiosity or attention.
